proofs.proof_tex:
Fix an arm and suppress its subscript.  Write \(\eta=\log\pi=\alpha\log d+g\),
\(Z_J=(\log d,B_{1,J},\ldots,B_{J,J})^\top\), and
\[
 \langle v,w\rangle_I=E_P\!\left[\frac{\pi(X)}{1-\pi(X)}v(X)w(X)\right].
\tag{1}
\]
The upper probability constraint, \(\text{ass:opposite-overlap}\), and compactness make the denominator harmless on the population neighborhood below.  The special value at the single endpoint enters neither a population integral nor, by \(\text{ass:uniform-chart}\), the sample likelihood with positive probability.

We first derive the deterministic sieve bounds.  Cellwise Taylor polynomials patched by the degree-\(r\) B-splines give \(g_J\) with
\[
 \|g-g_J\|_\infty\le C J^{-s}.
\tag{2}
\]
The Hall condition and boundedness of \(g\) imply, for small \(u\),
\[
 C_1u^{\gamma-1}\le P\{d(X)^\alpha\le u\}\le C_2u^{\gamma-1},
 \qquad \alpha=(\gamma-1)^{-1}.
\tag{3}
\]
Thus the increasing quantile \(Q_\pi(v)\) satisfies \(Q_\pi(v)\ge Cv^\alpha\).  For any measurable set \(C_0\) of measure at least \(c/J\),
\[
 \int_{C_0}\pi(x)\,dx\ge\int_0^{c/J}Q_\pi(v)\,dv\ge C J^{-(\alpha+1)}.
\tag{4}
\]
On each knot cell, finite-dimensional norm equivalence supplies a subset of fixed relative measure on which a degree-\(r\) polynomial exceeds a fixed multiple of its coefficient norm.  Applying (4), using local support, and profiling \(\log d\) against the spline space gives
\[
 cJ^{-(\alpha+1)}\|v\|_2^2
 \le\left\|\sum_jv_jB_{j,J}\right\|_I^2\le CJ^{-1}\|v\|_2^2,
\tag{5}
\]
\[
 \lambda_{\min}E_P\!\left[\frac{\pi(X)}{1-\pi(X)}Z_JZ_J^\top\right]
 \ge cJ^{-(\alpha+1)}.
\tag{6}
\]
For (6), partition the level sets in (3) into \(J\) probability blocks and apply polynomial norm equivalence to the residual of \(\log d\) on each block.  The exponential tail of \(-\log d\) following from (3), together with \(2r+1>\alpha\), makes every moment used below finite.  The constants are uniform because the Hölder radii, Hall envelopes, validity thresholds, and parameter bounds are common over \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm S}\).

Let \(\eta_J\) be the population sieve maximizer.  Population-score Taylor expansion around the approximant in (2), followed by (5)--(6), yields
\[
 \sup_{d(x)\ge n^{-b_0}}|\eta_J(x)-\eta(x)|
 \le C J^{-s}(\log n)^C.
\tag{7}
\]
For a direction \(v\), the centered likelihood score is the sum of the mean-zero variables
\[
 \frac{\{\mathbf1(A=a)-\pi(X)\}v(X)}{1-\pi(X)}.
\]
Truncate at \(|\log d|\le C\log n\).  Exponential Markov bounds for the bounded truncation and (3), followed by a union bound over the \(J+1\) coordinates, give
\[
 |(\mathbb P_{-k}-P)s_v|
 \le C(\log n)^C\{n^{-1/2}\|v\|_I+n^{-1}\|v\|_\infty\}.
\tag{8}
\]
Applying the same calculation to locally supported basis products gives
\[
 \sup_{\|v\|_I=1}|(\mathbb P_{-k}-P)\{\pi(1-\pi)^{-1}v^2\}|=o_P(1),
\tag{9}
\]
because \(J^{\alpha+1}\log n/n\to0\).  Taylor's formula for
\(\log(1-e^u)\), (8)--(9), strict concavity from the ridge, and the likelihood basic inequality now imply
\[
 \sup_{d(x)\ge n^{-b_0}}|\widehat\eta_{-k}(x)-\eta(x)|
 =O_P\!\left[(\log n)^C\{J^{-s}+(J^{\alpha+1}/n)^{1/2}\}\right].
\tag{10}
\]
If a constraint is active, its normal-cone inner product with the displacement toward \(\eta_J\) is nonpositive, so the same bound holds.  This proves the log-error assertion.

For \(L_\tau(v)=\int m_\tau v\,dP_X\), let \(r_{\tau,J}\) be its Riesz representer on the sieve under (1).  On boundary cell \(j\), \(\pi\) has order \((j/J)^\alpha\) in the rearrangement sense of (4), while a normalized local spline has integral of order \(J^{-1}\).  Cellwise Cauchy--Schwarz and \(\sum_{j\ge1}j^{-\alpha}<\infty\) give
\[
 \|r_{\tau,J}\|_I^2\le C J^{\alpha-1}.
\tag{11}
\]
Expanding \(e^{\widehat\eta-\eta}\), using (8) in the single Riesz direction, (2), and (9), gives
\[
 \int m_\tau(x)\frac{\widehat\pi_{-k}(x)-\pi(x)}{\pi(x)}\,dP_X(x)
 =O_P\!\left((\log n)^C
 \{J^{-s}+n^{-1/2}J^{(\alpha-1)/2}+J^\alpha/n\}\right).
\tag{12}
\]
The final term is the integrated exponential Taylor remainder.  The same cell calculation without the linear functional gives
\[
 \int\left\{\frac{\widehat\pi_{-k}(x)-\pi(x)}{\pi(x)}\right\}^2dP_X(x)
 =O_P\!\left((\log n)^C\{J^{-2s}+J^\alpha/n\}\right).
\tag{13}
\]
This proves both likelihood-functional assertions.

By (3), \(P\{d(X)<n^{-b_0}\}\le Cn^{-b_0}\).  Since \(b_0>1\), iid sampling and a union bound show that no sample point lies there with probability tending to one.  Hence (10) gives
\(E_{a,n}=O_P((\log n)^C\delta_{a,n})\).  Choose deterministic \(M_n\uparrow\infty\) slowly enough that
\[
 (\log n)^C\delta_{a,n}M_n^{\gamma_a-1}\to0.
\tag{14}
\]
On \(\{\pi>u=M_n/h\}\), clipping is inactive with probability tending to one.  Conditional on the training sample, decompose \(D_{a,n}\) into mean and centered parts and use
\[
 \widehat\pi^{-1}-\pi^{-1}
 =-\frac{\widehat\pi-\pi}{\pi^2}
 +\frac{(\widehat\pi-\pi)^2}{\pi^2\widehat\pi}.
\tag{15}
\]
Equations (12)--(13) bound the conditional mean by
\[
 \frac n h\{J^{-s}+n^{-1/2}J^{(\alpha-1)/2}+J^\alpha/n\}(\log n)^C+o_P(1).
\tag{16}
\]
The removed band contributes at most
\(CE_{a,n}M_n^{\gamma-1}=o_P(1)\), since Hall integration and the generalized inverse give \(c_an h^{-\gamma}\to1\).  The conditional variance of the centered part is bounded by (13) times the corresponding truncated inverse-propensity integral and is \(o_P(1)\) after making \(M_n\) still slower.  With \(J=n^\xi\) and \(n/h\asymp n^{1/(\alpha+1)}\), every exponent in (16) is negative when
\[
 \frac1{s(\alpha+1)}<\xi<\frac1{\alpha+1}.
\]
Thus \(E_{a,n}M_n^{\gamma_a-1}=o_P(1)\) and
\(\max_{\tau\in\mathcal T}|D_{a,n}(\tau)|=o_P(1)\).

At \(\alpha=s=3/2\), \(J=n^{3/10}\), (10) has exponent \(-1/8\).  The three exponents in (12) are \(-18/40,-17/40,-22/40\), and multiplication by \(n/h\asymp n^{2/5}\) gives \(-1/40\).  These are the asserted numerical orders.

Here \(\pi_0(x)=1-x^{3/2}/2\), so direct inversion gives
\[
F_0^\pi(t)=
\begin{cases}
0,&t\le1/2,\\
1-\{2(1-t)\}^{2/3},&1/2<t<1,\\
1,&t\ge1.
\end{cases}
\tag{17}
\]
Thus \(F_0^\pi(1/2+v)=4v/3+O(v^2)\), and the equation
\(ntF_0^\pi(t)=1\) gives
\[
t_{0,n}=\frac12+\frac{3}{2n}+O(n^{-2}),\qquad h_{0,n}\to2.
\tag{18}
\]

Let \(V_J=\operatorname{span}(\mathcal B_J)\), and let \(r_J\) be the residual after profiling \(\log(1-x)\) against \(V_J\) in Bernoulli information norm.  On the final knot cell, the change \(u=J(1-x)\) leaves the nonpolynomial part \(\log u\), while \(-\log J\) is absorbed by the constant spline.  Norm equivalence and the fact that \(\log u\) is not a degree-\(r\) polynomial give
\[
\|r_J\|_I^2\asymp J^{-1}.
\tag{19}
\]
Taylor approximation of the smooth true log propensity on that cell and the defining orthogonality give the population profiled coefficient
\[
\alpha_J=O(J^{-s}).
\tag{20}
\]
The profiled score has standard deviation of order \((N\|r_J\|_I^2)^{1/2}\), while its negative derivative has order \(N\|r_J\|_I^2\).  The bounded Bernoulli exponential-moment calculation therefore yields
\[
\widehat\alpha_{-k}-\alpha_J=O_P\{\sqrt{J/N}\}.
\tag{21}
\]
The corresponding local-spline score calculation and inverse inequality give
\[
\|\widehat g_{-k}^{\rm prof}-g_J^{\rm prof}\|_\infty
=O_P\{\sqrt{J\log J/N}+J^{-s}\}.
\tag{22}
\]
The uniform design and a union bound for the distance of evaluation points from the endpoint, combined with the last-cell representation, give
\[
\max_{i\in I_k}|r_J(X_i)|=O_P\{\log(N/J)\}.
\tag{23}
\]
Combining (20)--(23), over finitely many folds,
\[
\max_i|\widehat\eta_{0,-k(i)}(X_i)-\eta_0(X_i)|
=O_P\!\left\{\sqrt{J/N}\log(N/J)+J^{-s}\log(N/J)
+\sqrt{J\log J/N}+J^{-s}\right\}=o_P(1).
\tag{24}
\]
Indeed, \(J\log N/N\to0\) implies \(J/N\to0\) and
\(\sqrt{J/N}\log(N/J)\to0\), since \(\sqrt x\log(1/x)\to0\); the separately added condition handles the approximation term.  Exponentiation on the bounded true range now gives
\[
\max_i|\widehat\pi_{0,-k(i)}(X_i)-\pi_0(X_i)|=o_P(1).
\tag{25}
\]

The fitted empirical distribution is consequently sandwiched between translates of the empirical distribution of the true propensities.  Indicator variances and (17) imply convergence at every continuity point, so the generalized inverse and (18) yield
\(\widehat h_{0,n}\to_P2\).  Every fixed lower order statistic of the true propensities tends to \(1/2\); the tight rank
\(\lceil\widehat h_{0,n}\rceil\) and (25) therefore give
\[
\widehat p_{0,(\lceil\widehat h_{0,n}\rceil)}\to_P\frac12,\qquad
\widehat b_{0,n}\to_P\frac{\vartheta_0}{2}<\frac12,
\tag{26}
\]
where \(\vartheta_0\le\bar\vartheta<1\).

Because \(k_n/n\to0\), (17) and (25) also imply
\(\max_{j\le k_n+1}|Z_{0,(j)}-2|=o_P(1)\).  Hence the nonnegative Hill log-spacing average tends to zero and its reciprocal diverges under the declared convention:
\(\widehat\gamma_0\to_P\infty\).  The arm is classified as Gaussian and its drift is zero with probability tending to one.  Finally, (25)--(26) imply
\(\min_i\widehat\pi_{0,-k(i)}(X_i)>\widehat b_{0,n}\) with probability tending to one, so every clipped weight equals its untrimmed fitted weight.

Fix a heavy arm.  Hall inversion gives
\[
t_{a,n}=(c_an)^{-1/\gamma_a}\{1+o(1)\},\quad
h_{a,n}=(c_an)^{1/\gamma_a}\{1+o(1)\},\quad
c_an h_{a,n}^{-\gamma_a}\to1.
\tag{27}
\]
The tail-band relative likelihood bound sandwiches fitted tail counts between true counts with multiplicatively perturbed arguments.  At \(t=z/h_{a,n}\), the true expected count is asymptotic to \(h_{a,n}z^{\gamma_a-1}\), and its variance is no larger than its mean.  Uniform Hall inversion and monotonicity thus give
\[
\widehat h_{a,n}/h_{a,n}\to_P1,\qquad
h_{a,n}\widehat p_{a,(\lceil\widehat h_{a,n}\rceil)}\to_P1,\qquad
\widehat h_{a,n}\widehat b_{a,n}\to_P\vartheta_a=\theta_a.
\tag{28}
\]

Put \(z=h_{a,n}\pi_a(X)\) and \(u=\Psi_a(Y(a))\).  Treatment thins the covariate tail by \(z/h_{a,n}\).  Thus iid sampling, (27), Hall regular variation, consistency, unconfoundedness, and \(\text{lem:score-law-factorization}\) imply, for compactly supported bounded continuous \(g\),
\[
nE_P[\mathbf1(A=a)g\{h_{a,n}\pi_a(X),\Psi_a(Y)\}]
\to\int_0^\infty\!\int g(z,u)H_a(du)(\gamma_a-1)z^{\gamma_a-1}dz.
\tag{29}
\]
Expanding the iid Laplace transform proves marked point-process convergence.  Compensation then gives
\[
S_{a,n}-E_PS_{a,n}\Rightarrow\mathsf Z_{a,\theta},\qquad
S_{a,n}(\tau)=h_{a,n}^{-1}\sum_i
\frac{\mathbf1(A_i=a)\psi_{a,\tau}(Y_i)}{\pi_a(X_i)\vee b_{a,n}}.
\tag{30}
\]
Near zero, the compensated first moment is integrable because \(\gamma_a>1\); at infinity, the second-order bound is proportional to \(z^{\gamma_a-3}\), integrable because \(\gamma_a<2\).

Since \(E_Pm_{a,\tau}(X)=E_P\psi_{a,\tau}\{Y(a)\}=0\), Hall integration gives
\[
E_PS_{a,n}(\tau)\to-\theta_a^{\gamma_a-1}m^{\rm tail}_{a,\tau}/\gamma_a
=\mu_{a,\theta}(\tau),
\tag{31}
\]
using
\((\gamma-1)\int_0^\theta(z/\theta-1)z^{\gamma-2}dz=-\theta^{\gamma-1}/\gamma\).

Knight's identity,
\[
\rho_\tau(e-v)-\rho_\tau(e)
=-v\psi_{a,\tau}(q_a(\tau)+e)
+\int_0^v\{\mathbf1(e\le s)-\mathbf1(e\le0)\}\,ds,
\tag{32}
\]
with \(v=th_{a,n}/n\), and the conditional density modulus show uniformly on compact \(t\)-sets that the oracle objective is
\[
\frac12f_a(\tau)t^2-t\{\mathsf Z_{a,\theta}(\tau)+\mu_{a,\theta}(\tau)\}+o_P(1).
\tag{33}
\]
The centered curvature variance is \(O(|t|^3h_{a,n}/n)=o(1)\).

For the feasible score, the reciprocal identity and the definition of \(D_{a,n}\) give
\[
\max_\tau|S^{\rm fe}_{a,n}(\tau)-S^{\rm or}_{a,n}(\tau)|
\le CE_{a,n}h_{a,n}^{-1}\sum_i
\frac{\mathbf1\{A_i=a,\pi_a(X_i)\le M_n/h_{a,n}\}}
{\pi_a(X_i)\vee b_{a,n}}+\max_\tau|D_{a,n}(\tau)|+o_P(1).
\tag{34}
\]
Hall integration makes the normalized sum \(O_P(M_n^{\gamma_a-1})\); the two likelihood-lemma conditions make (34) \(o_P(1)\).  Its square-integral bound similarly transfers the curvature.

Positive curvature localizes the smallest convex minimizer, so
\[
\frac n{h_{a,n}}(\widehat q_a-q_a)
\Rightarrow(\mathsf Z_{a,\theta}+\mu_{a,\theta})/f_a.
\tag{35}
\]
We now verify the empirical correction.  At
\(t_{a,k}=F_a^{\pi,-1}(k_n/n)\),
\[
t_{a,k}\asymp(k_n/n)^{1/(\gamma_a-1)},\qquad
nE_P[\mathbf1\{A=a,\pi_a(X)\le t_{a,k}\}]
\asymp k_nt_{a,k}\to\infty.
\tag{36}
\]
The sample-point likelihood bound permits replacement of fitted by true intermediate order statistics.  Integrating the tail empirical survival function shows that the Hill average tends to \((\gamma_a-1)^{-1}\), hence
\(\widehat\gamma_a\to_P\gamma_a\).  Equation (36), the mark modulus, and inner-fold consistency from (35) give
\(\widehat m^{\rm tail}_{a,\tau}\to_Pm^{\rm tail}_{a,\tau}\).

For the density estimate, its denominator divided by \(n\) tends to one.  The bounded probability-kernel approximate-identity calculation, the density modulus, and the vanishing clipping-tail mass make the numerator expectation tend to \(f_a(\tau)\).  Its variance is bounded by
\[
\frac C{n\omega_{a,n}}E_P\!\left[
\frac{\pi_a(X)}{\{\pi_a(X)\vee b_{a,n}\}^2}\right]
=O\!\left(\frac{h_{a,n}^{2-\gamma_a}}{n\omega_{a,n}}\right)=o(1).
\tag{37}
\]
Also \(|\widehat q_a-q_a|/\omega_{a,n}
=O_P\{h_{a,n}/(n\omega_{a,n})\}=o_P(1)\).  Therefore
\(\widehat f_a\to_Pf_a\) and, with (28) and (36),
\(\widehat\mu_{a,\theta}\to_P\mu_{a,\theta}\).  Subtracting the empirical drift in \(\text{def:drift-correction}\) from (35) proves
\[
\left(\frac n{h_{a,n}}\{\widehat q_a^{\rm bc}(\tau)-q_a(\tau)\}\right)_{\tau\in\mathcal T}
\Rightarrow\left(\frac{\mathsf Z_{a,\theta}(\tau)}{f_a(\tau)}\right)_{\tau\in\mathcal T}.
\]
Using true propensities and the population clip simply removes (34), so it recovers the asserted oracle law.  The mark dependence is only through \(H_a\) by the score-law lemma.

Fix the treated arm of the nonzero-drift mixed witness and set
\(\gamma=\gamma_a\), \(h=h_{a,n}\), \(u=M_n/h\), and
\(\epsilon_n=M_n^{-(\gamma-1)}\).  The likelihood lemma gives
\(E_{a,n}=o_P(\epsilon_n)\), and oracle preservation gives
\(\widehat h_{a,n}/h\to_P1\).  Strictly inside the fitted tail band,
\[
\frac{\widehat\pi^{\rm esc}_{a,-k}}{\pi_a}-1
=(1+\epsilon_n)\left(1+\frac{\widehat\pi_{a,-k}-\pi_a}{\pi_a}\right)-1
=\epsilon_n+o_P(\epsilon_n).
\tag{38}
\]
The number of points with \(\pi_a(X_i)\le u/2\) has mean of order
\(hM_n^{\gamma-1}\to\infty\) and variance no larger than its mean.  Thus
\[
E^{\rm esc}_{a,n}M_n^{\gamma-1}\to_P1.
\tag{39}
\]
Above \(u\), the rules differ only on an \(o_P(1)\)-relative shell.  Hall integration over it, multiplied by \(\epsilon_n\), is \(o_P(1)\); since \(D_{a,n}\to_P0\), this proves \(D^{\rm esc}_{a,n}\to_P0\).  On every fixed window \(h\pi_a\le C\), the multiplier tends uniformly to one, preserving the endpoint mark limit.

For fixed \(C>\theta_a\), clipping is inactive on
\(C/h<\pi_a<M_n/h\).  Conditional on training folds, the mean difference of the normalized linear scores is
\[
-\frac{\epsilon_n n}{h}\{1+o_P(1)\}
\int_{C/h}^{M_n/h}\kappa_{a,\tau}(t)\,dF_a^\pi(t).
\tag{40}
\]
The mark modulus and Hall expansion make the integral
\[
m^{\rm tail}_{a,\tau}c_ah^{-(\gamma-1)}
\{M_n^{\gamma-1}-C^{\gamma-1}\}\{1+o(1)\}.
\]
Because \(\epsilon_nM_n^{\gamma-1}=1\), \(c_an h^{-\gamma}\to1\), and
\(\epsilon_nC^{\gamma-1}\to0\), (40) tends to
\(-m^{\rm tail}_{a,\tau}\).  Its centered conditional variance is at most
\[
C_1\epsilon_n^2\frac n{h^2}\int_{C/h}^{M_n/h}t^{-1}\,dF_a^\pi(t)+o_P(1)
=O_P(\epsilon_n^2C^{\gamma-2})+o_P(1)=o_P(1).
\]
The fixed clipped window is a tight score multiplied by \(\epsilon_n\), so, jointly over finite \(\mathcal T\),
\[
S_n^{\rm esc}-S_n\to_P-m_a^{\rm tail}.
\tag{41}
\]
The intermediate-band drift ingredients are unchanged to first order, and common multiplicative factors cancel from Hill spacings.  The positive-curvature argmin expansion gives
\[
\frac n{h_{a,n}}\{\widehat q_a^{\rm bc,esc}(\tau)
-\widehat q_a^{\rm bc}(\tau)\}
\to_P-\frac{m^{\rm tail}_{a,\tau}}{f_a(\tau)}.
\]
The endpoint score is nonzero on the mixed witness.  Hence exact order
\(M_n^{-(\gamma_a-1)}\) changes the normalized limit despite fixed-window preservation, proving intrinsic necessity.

Fix a Gaussian arm and a quantile index.  Differentiation of the Bernoulli log-link likelihood in a log-propensity direction \(g\) gives
\[
s_g(O)=\frac{\{\mathbf1(A=a)-\pi_a(X)\}g(X)}{1-\pi_a(X)},\qquad
\mathcal I_a(g_1,g_2)=E_P\!\left[
\frac{\pi_a(X)}{1-\pi_a(X)}g_1(X)g_2(X)\right].
\tag{42}
\]
The derivative of the signed functional is
\(\dot L_a(g)=E_P\{m_{a,\tau}(X)g(X)\}\), whose Riesz representer is
\[
r_{a,\tau}(X)=m_{a,\tau}(X)\frac{1-\pi_a(X)}{\pi_a(X)}.
\tag{43}
\]
Indeed, substitution in (42) gives
\(\mathcal I_a(r_{a,\tau},g)=\dot L_a(g)\).  Moreover,
\[
E_Ps_{r_{a,\tau}}^2
=E_P\!\left[m_{a,\tau}(X)^2\frac{1-\pi_a(X)}{\pi_a(X)}\right]<\infty
\tag{44}
\]
by \(\text{ass:finite-variance}\) and \(|m_{a,\tau}|\le1\).

Let \(r_{a,\tau,J}\) be the information projection of (43) on the likelihood sieve.  Truncate (43), approximate the truncation by splines, and remove the truncation using (44); this proves
\(s_{r_{a,\tau,J}}\to s_{r_{a,\tau}}\) in \(L^2(P)\).  The score and random-Hessian derivation (5)--(13), now with \(\alpha_a<1\), gives
\[
\sqrt n\,\text{(product approximation bias)}=O(\sqrt nJ_n^{-2s}),\qquad
\sqrt n\,\text{(reciprocal quadratic remainder)}
=O_P(J_n^{\alpha_a}/\sqrt n),
\tag{45}
\]
and the Hessian replacement is \(o_P(1)\) under
\(J_n^{\alpha_a+1}\log n/n\to0\).  For a bounded-away arm, profiling the redundant \(\log d_a\) direction gives (19)--(24): the added condition controls the approximation term, and \(J_n\log n/n\to0\), which is the fourth tuning condition at \(\alpha_a=0\), controls the stochastic term.  No raw coordinatewise supremum convergence of the spline coefficient vector is invoked.

For every fold, the likelihood score equation, (42)--(45), and the favorable sign of an active constraint's normal-cone term yield
\[
\sqrt n\sum_{k=1}^K\frac{|I_k|}{n}
\int m_{a,\tau}(x)
\frac{\widehat\pi_{a,-k}(x)-\pi_a(x)}{\pi_a(x)}\,dP_X(x)
=\frac1{\sqrt n}\sum_{i=1}^n s_{r_{a,\tau}}(O_i)+o_P(1).
\tag{46}
\]
The coefficient on the right is one: every observation belongs to \(K-1\) training samples, each of asymptotic size \(n(K-1)/K\).  Cross-fitting makes the centered evaluation replacement have conditional variance at most
\(C\int(\widehat\eta-\eta)^2/\pi_a\,dP_X=o_P(1)\).  Cellwise calculation gives order
\(J_n^{-2s}+J_n^{2\alpha_a}/n\), which vanishes since
\(2\alpha_a<\alpha_a+1\).

Clipping is first-order negligible.  If the propensity is bounded away from zero, (24) makes it inactive.  If \(2<\gamma_a<\infty\), Hall integration gives
\[
\sqrt n\left|E_Pm_{a,\tau}(X)
\left\{\frac{\pi_a(X)}{\pi_a(X)\vee b_{a,n}}-1\right\}\right|
=O\{n^{1/2-(\gamma_a-1)/\gamma_a}\}=o(1),
\tag{47}
\]
and the centered clipping difference has variance tending to zero by uniform integrability of \(1/\pi_a(X)\).  The tail-count sandwich used in (28) permits the empirical threshold to replace the population one.

Knight's identity with \(v=t/\sqrt n\) and the density modulus give the local objective
\[
\frac12f_a(\tau)t^2-t\,n^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^n
\left[\frac{\mathbf1(A_i=a)\psi_{a,\tau}(Y_i)}{\pi_a(X_i)}
-s_{r_{a,\tau}}(O_i)\right]+o_P(1).
\tag{48}
\]
Using (43), the bracket equals
\[
m_{a,\tau}(X_i)+\frac{\mathbf1(A_i=a)
\{\psi_{a,\tau}(Y_i)-m_{a,\tau}(X_i)\}}{\pi_a(X_i)}
=f_a(\tau){\rm IF}_a(O_i;\tau).
\tag{49}
\]
It has finite second moment by (44).  Truncating the finite arm--quantile vector, expanding its iid characteristic function, and then removing the truncation proves its multivariate Gaussian limit with covariance equal to the influence-function outer-product expectation.  The positive density lower bound localizes the convex minimizer.  Equations (48)--(49) prove the claimed joint linear representation.

The definition of \(\widehat\Delta^{\rm bc}\) gives
\[
\frac n{H_n}(\widehat\Delta^{\rm bc}-\Delta)
=\ell_{1,n}\frac n{H_{1,n}}(\widehat q_1^{\rm bc}-q_1)
-\ell_{0,n}\frac n{H_{0,n}}(\widehat q_0^{\rm bc}-q_0).
\tag{50}
\]
The armwise limits are \(\text{thm:oracle-preservation}\) and
\(\text{thm:gaussian-branch}\).  Their two remainders are jointly \(o_P(1)\); along \(\ell_{a,n}\to\ell_a\), (50) proves the displayed limit.

For a heavy arm, (27) gives
\(h_{a,n}=(c_an)^{1/\gamma_a}\{1+o(1)\}\).  If
\(\gamma_1<\gamma_0<2\), then
\[
\frac{h_{1,n}}{h_{0,n}}
=\frac{c_1^{1/\gamma_1}}{c_0^{1/\gamma_0}}
n^{1/\gamma_1-1/\gamma_0}\{1+o(1)\}\to\infty,
\]
so the smaller index dominates.  Equal indices give ratio
\((c_1/c_0)^{1/\gamma}\), retaining both arms.  Also
\(h_{a,n}/\sqrt n\to\infty\) when \(\gamma_a<2\), proving heavy-over-Gaussian dominance.  With two Gaussian arms, both normalizations are \(\sqrt n\), and (49) retains their shared influence-function covariance.

For two heavy arms, binary propensity coherence and
\(\text{ass:opposite-overlap}\) give disjoint endpoint neighborhoods.  For compactly supported nonnegative test functions \(g_0,g_1\), iid sampling gives the joint Laplace transform
\[
\left[1-\frac{\nu_{0,n}(1-e^{-g_0})}{n}
-\frac{\nu_{1,n}(1-e^{-g_1})}{n}+o(n^{-1})\right]^n.
\]
The rare events cannot occur for the same observation, so no cross term of order \(n^{-1}\) appears.  Hall and mark convergence make the limit
\[
\exp\{-\nu_0(1-e^{-g_0})\}\exp\{-\nu_1(1-e^{-g_1})\}.
\]
This factorization proves independence of the endpoint Poisson limits.  Joint \(o_P(1)\) oracle-transfer errors preserve it.

Fix \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm S}\), and write all vectors in dimension \(R=|\mathcal T|\).  At arbitrary sample size \(N\), Hall inversion gives
\[
H_{a,N}=(c_aN)^{1/\gamma_a}\{1+o(1)\}
\quad(a\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm H}),\qquad
H_{a,N}=\sqrt N\quad(a\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm G}).
\tag{51}
\]
Define
\[
W_{N,a}^{\circ}=\frac N{\widehat H_{a,N}}
\{\widehat q_{a,N}^{\rm bc}-q_a\}.
\]
The heavy and Gaussian expansions, with their tuning conditions at size \(N\), imply
\[
W_N^\circ\Rightarrow(L_0,L_1),\qquad
\widehat H_{a,N}/H_{a,N}\to_P1.
\tag{52}
\]
They also give a permutation-symmetric leading statistic \(S_N\), the compensated oracle statistic for a heavy arm and the normalized influence-function sum for a Gaussian arm, such that
\[
\|W_N^\circ-S_N\|\to_P0,\qquad S_N\Rightarrow(L_0,L_1).
\tag{53}
\]

For bounded Lipschitz \(g:\mathbb R^{2R}\to\mathbb R\), put
\[
U_{n,m}(g)=\binom nm^{-1}\sum_{|b|=m}g(S_b)
=E_B\{g(S_B)\mid O_1,\ldots,O_n\}.
\]
Center the symmetric kernel and successively subtract all lower-order conditional expectations, obtaining orthogonal degenerate projections
\[
g(S_m)-Eg(S_m)=\sum_{j=1}^m\sum_{|C|=j}h_{m,j}(O_C).
\]
If \(\zeta_{m,j}=Eh_{m,j}(O_1,\ldots,O_j)^2\), independence and counting the \(m\)-subsets containing a fixed \(j\)-subset give
\[
\operatorname{Var}\{U_{n,m}(g)\}
=\sum_{j=1}^m\frac{\binom mj^2}{\binom nj}\zeta_{m,j}
\le\frac mn\operatorname{Var}\{g(S_m)\}
\le4\|g\|_\infty^2\frac mn.
\tag{54}
\]
Since \(m/n\to0\), (53)--(54) and
\(EU_{n,m}(g)=Eg(S_m)\to Eg(L_0,L_1)\) imply
\[
E_B\{g(S_B)\mid O_1,\ldots,O_n\}\to_PEg(L_0,L_1).
\tag{55}
\]
A countable dense family of bounded Lipschitz functions, followed by approximation, turns (55) into conditional weak convergence in probability.

A uniform \(m\)-subset of an iid sample has the unconditional law of \(m\) iid observations.  Therefore, for every \(\epsilon>0\),
\[
E\!\left[P_B\{\|W_B^\circ-S_B\|>\epsilon\mid O_1,\ldots,O_n\}\right]
=P\{\|W_m^\circ-S_m\|>\epsilon\}\to0.
\]
Markov's inequality and (55) prove
\[
\mathcal L_B(W_B^\circ\mid O_1,\ldots,O_n)
\Rightarrow_P\mathcal L(L_0,L_1).
\tag{56}
\]

By definition,
\[
V_{B,a}=W_{B,a}^\circ-C_{B,a},\qquad
C_{B,a}=\frac m{\widehat H_{a,m,B}}\{\widehat q_a^{\rm bc}-q_a\}.
\tag{57}
\]
Equation (52) at \(n\) and \(m\), followed by the same conditional Markov argument, gives, for a heavy arm,
\[
\|C_{B,a}\|=O_P\!\left(\frac m{H_{a,m}}\frac{H_{a,n}}n\right)
=O_P\{(m/n)^{1-1/\gamma_a}\}=o_P(1),
\tag{58}
\]
and, for a Gaussian arm,
\[
\|C_{B,a}\|=O_P\{(m/n)^{1/2}\}=o_P(1).
\tag{59}
\]
Gamma separation makes these bounds simultaneous.  Scale consistency gives
\(\widehat\ell_{a,n}-\ell_{a,n}\to_P0\).  Conditional Slutsky applied to (56)--(59) proves
\[
\mathcal L_B(T_{B,n}\mid O_1,\ldots,O_n)
\Rightarrow_P\mathcal L(\ell_1L_1-\ell_0L_0).
\tag{60}
\]

Fix \(\tau\) and write \(Z_\tau=\ell_1L_1(\tau)-\ell_0L_0(\tau)\).
Anti-concentration makes its distribution continuous at the needed quantiles.  Thus (60) gives
\[
c_{n,p}(\tau)\to_Pc_p(\tau),\qquad
p\in\{\alpha/2,1-\alpha/2\}.
\tag{61}
\]
The joint QTE theorem and \(\widehat H_n/H_n\to_P1\) give
\[
\frac n{\widehat H_n}\{\widehat\Delta^{\rm bc}(\tau)-\Delta(\tau)\}
\Rightarrow Z_\tau.
\tag{62}
\]
The interval covers exactly when (62) lies between the quantiles in (61); continuity proves limiting coverage \(1-\alpha\).  Finiteness of \(\mathcal T\) makes the maximum coordinatewise coverage error tend to zero.

For the nonuniformity certificate, choose interior \(1<\gamma<2\), \(c>0\), and the two-heavy family in \(\text{prop:smooth-inclusion}\), with equal Hall constants and nondegenerate endpoint limits.  Put
\[
\gamma_{0,n}=\gamma+\frac c{2\log n},\qquad
\gamma_{1,n}=\gamma-\frac c{2\log n}.
\tag{63}
\]
The exponents remain in a common compact permitted by gamma separation, so the row laws remain in \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm S}\) with common constants.  From (51),
\[
\log\frac{h_{0,n}}{h_{1,n}}
=\left(\frac1{\gamma_{0,n}}-\frac1{\gamma_{1,n}}\right)\log n+o(1)
\to-\frac c{\gamma^2}.
\tag{64}
\]
The row-wise law therefore retains \(L_1-e^{-c/\gamma^2}L_0\).  Holding a row law fixed and sending a fresh sample size to infinity instead eliminates the larger-index arm and yields \(L_1\).  Independence and nondegeneracy distinguish these laws: equality of characteristic functions near zero would force the characteristic function of the nonzero multiple of \(L_0\) to equal one there, hence \(L_0=0\) almost surely.  A bounded Lipschitz function separates them, proving nonuniformity.

If \(m=n^\beta\), \(0<\beta<1\), the same calculation gives
\[
\log\frac{h_{0,m}}{h_{1,m}}\to-\frac{\beta c}{\gamma^2}.
\tag{65}
\]
Raw scalar subsampling therefore converges to
\(L_1-e^{-\beta c/\gamma^2}L_0\), not the full-sample mixture in (64).  The arm-vector rule estimates both coordinates at their \(m\)-scales and recombines them with full-sample weights \(\widehat\ell_{a,n}\), which reproduce (64).  This proves the final assertion.

prose_updates.tldr: A boundary-adapted growing Bernoulli likelihood preserves the compensated infinitely divisible clipped-IPW quantile law under Hall weak overlap.  The signed Riesz expansion gives the rate \(J_n^{-s}+n^{-1/2}J_n^{(\alpha_a-1)/2}+J_n^{\alpha_a}/n\) and derives the amplified transfer condition.  Profiling the redundant boundary direction also proves bounded-arm sample-point consistency under the added approximation-tail condition, which is imposed at both full-sample and refitted subsample sizes.  The resulting procedure has heavy, Gaussian, joint unequal-tail, and conditionally valid arm-vector subsampling laws; the critical fold-labelled Poisson question remains separate.

project_justification.gap: The closest weak-overlap QTE theorem uses the observed true propensity.  Regular estimated-propensity quantile and series-logit results do not supply the singular Hall-boundary signed-functional expansion, empirical clipping correction, or mixed-rate arm recombination proved here.
project_justification.niche: A feasible full-population QTE estimator needs a likelihood expansion that preserves signed cancellation at a Hall boundary, a positive-weight convex argmin, a consistently estimated clipping drift, and shared first-stage covariance.
project_justification.fill: The project derives the constrained-sieve log and signed-functional rates, proves the amplified oracle-transfer condition and its escape-perturbation necessity, establishes profiled bounded-arm sample-point consistency without raw coefficient sup convergence, derives heavy and Gaussian arm laws, recombines unequal arm scales, and validates fully refitted arm-vector subsampling.

sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Fixed-fold constrained Bernoulli series likelihood with a boundary exponent profiled against a quasi-uniform spline space.  The schedules retain \(J_N\log N/N\to0\) and additionally impose \(J_N^{-s}\log(N/J_N)\to0\) at \(N=n\) and at every refit size \(N=m\).  Generalized-inverse scales, order-statistic clips, Hill classification, preliminary quantiles, endpoint scores, drift corrections, and densities are all recomputed from the relevant sample.

prose_updates.related_work: Avella-Medina, Davis, and Samorodnitsky (2025, arXiv:2506.18215v1) provide the observed true-propensity fixed-quantile benchmark but no feasible propensity-estimation theorem.  Hirano, Imbens, and Ridder (2003) motivate regular growing-likelihood projection; the proof here adds singular Hall-boundary information geometry and the signed Riesz rate.  Firpo (2007) supplies the regular QTE context, while the present Gaussian branch permits finite inverse moments and retains shared first-stage covariance.  Heiler and Kazak (2021) motivate irregular subsampling, whereas the proved procedure refits two convex arm estimators and recombines them at full-sample arm scales.  These are positioning comparisons, not claims that the cited papers contain the new expansions.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The theory remains separated from the exact boundary \(\gamma_a=2\), uses a fixed finite quantile set, and obtains uniform likelihood constants on the boundary-smooth subclass rather than the unrestricted Hall class.  The extra approximation-tail condition is required only for the profiled boundary approximation and is imposed after every subsample refit.  The endpoint restriction controls the finite nested score vector, not the full conditional outcome law.  The critical fold-labelled point-process law is not asserted here.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The proved contribution is the feasible transfer and inference theory: the constrained likelihood yields its explicit signed-functional rate and corrected amplified condition; the positive-weight argmin has a compensated heavy-arm law; the finite-variance branch has the displayed learned-propensity influence function; armwise recombination covers equal, unequal, and mixed regimes; and complete refitted arm-vector subsampling gives pointwise coverage for each reported quantile.  The bounded mixed control calculation explicitly profiles \(\log(1-x)\), derives sample-point consistency, fixed-rank clipping, divergent Hill classification, and zero drift.  Coverage is pointwise with simultaneous convergence of finitely many coordinatewise errors, not a simultaneous confidence band.  The critical fold-law OEQ remains open outside this unit.
